shortDescription: Dungeons from Alexander Wales' "This Used to Be About Dungeons": levelled sites across the world map that generate a fresh chamber-graph pocket map per party, stocked with Titan Framework creatures and Entad Framework rewards.
body:
## Status
Build order: 1 World → 2 Entry → 3 Map generation → 4 Creatures → 5 Rewards → 6 Vehicle Framework.
Phases 1 and 2 done. Phase 3 step 1 built (build 22), not yet tested in game.

## World (phase 1)
- `DungeonWorldComponent`: dungeons as plain data (surface tile id + level), saved as byte arrays, with `genVersion`, `generatedMaxLevel`. `enteredBy`: per tile, load ids of pawns who entered, cleared by Generate.
- Placement: seeded random order, BFS-blocked radius spacing-1. Land only unless Vehicle Framework + ocean setting.
- Levels: 3-octave Perlin over the unit sphere, ranked, level = 1 + floor(p^skew × max).
- `WorldDrawLayer_Dungeons`, bottom-right toggles, tile inspect line, world search, `Dialog_DungeonFinder`.

## Entry and leaving (phase 2)
- Enter via caravan gizmo, right-click on the tile, or forming a caravan toward it. `Dialog_EnterDungeon` splits the caravan; rules: one non-downed colonist, humanlikes ≤ cap, nobody who already entered.
- Party wealth = pawns + worn apparel + equipment. Effective level = level × (1 + wealth / wealthToDouble), stored on the site.
- `DungeonEntry.Enter` makes a `DungeonSite` (MapParent), generates the map, enters in front of the exit. `DungeonExit` (MapPortal) is a 3×1 stairway in the first chamber's north wall; `Dialog_LeaveDungeon` lists items to haul out. Map removed when no living player humanlike/mech remains; "party lost" letter.

## Map generation (phase 3)
Step 1 (built): `GenStep_DungeonLayout` + `DungeonLayoutGenerator` (Source/DungeonLayout.cs).
- Map side = lerp(60, 150) by the dungeon's own level over the world's max level (`DungeonEntry.MapSizeFor`). Wealth does not affect size.
- Layout seed is rolled per party (`site.layoutSeed`), so each party gets a new layout; MapGenerator's own seed would repeat.
- Chambers: rejection-sampled rectangles with ≥3 cells of wall between any two. Built rooms are full rectangles on PavedTile, cave pockets are star-shaped blobs on Gravel (35% of non-first chambers). Chamber 0 holds the exit and is always built.
- Passages: 1 cell wide, L-shaped between chamber centres; refused if they touch another chamber, passage or the exit area. Spanning tree from shortest feasible links, plus some loops. Unreachable chambers are dropped.
- Every passage has one divider at its middle: vanilla Door (wood) or `TUBAD_DungeonRubble` (Mineable, full fill, so it blocks sight). Fill = Full means MakeFog, so the room beyond stays fogged until the door opens or rubble is mined. Doors in the site use `doorsAlwaysOpenForPlayerPawns` so animals can pass.
- All remaining cells are `TUBAD_DungeonWall` (unbreakable), so there are no shortcuts. Thick rock roof everywhere for now.
- Saved on the site (`DungeonLayoutData`): chambers (rect, cave flag, depth, links), dividers (cell, type, the two chambers), exit cell.
Next steps: (2) `DungeonThemeDef` derived from biome (terrain lists, plant density, temperature/rainfall so modded biomes work), tile rock types, hilliness, rivers/coast, rare themes; (3) open-air variant bounded by cliffs, own-light vs dark dungeons, more divider types (vines/roots to cut, flooding).
Locked doors with keys/levers deferred; add a `Locked` divider type later.

## Settings (tabs)
- World: show icons, opacity, tint by level, spacing, max level, low level bias, roughness, ocean dungeons with VF.
- Parties: max party size 5, wealth that doubles the level 50,000.
- Planned: Creatures, Rewards.

## Agreed design (later phases)
- Phase 4 creatures via Titan: humanlikes, animals, insects, mechs if feasible; points from effective level; packs; tamable; suspended in undiscovered rooms. Toughness distribution is random, NOT tougher deeper in. Use chamber data for placement and dormancy only.
- Phase 5 rewards via EntadApi; binding single / party / unbound by settings.

## Textures
- World/TUBAD_Dungeon, World/TUBAD_Highlight, UI/TUBAD_ShowDungeons, UI/TUBAD_FindDungeons, Things/Building/TUBAD_DungeonExit, Things/Building/TUBAD_Rubble (placeholder SVGs).

## Mockups
- .circinus/mockups/dungeon-finder.html
